commit.message:
itest: wait for PSBT test channels to fully resolve

The unstable UTXO test sizes the replacement channel using the wallet's
anchor reserve. Confirming the to_remote sweep does not guarantee that
the wallet has stopped counting the force-closed channel. If PSBT
verification runs before full resolution, the wallet can reject the
funding transaction because it leaves too little for the anchor reserve.

In both halves of the test, wait until Carol reports no pending
force-close channels before funding the replacement channel.

Fixes #11645.

commit.message:
lncfg+itest: allow static remote key channels in integration builds

In this commit, we add a dev only option, --dev.allow-static-remote-key,
that lets an integration build open and accept new static remote key
channels. Production nodes still refuse them, but many of these channels
remain open in the wild, so the itests need a way to keep covering data
loss protection, SCB restore and watchtower justice for them.

The option lives in lncfg.DevConfig, whose production stub has no fields
and whose getter always returns false. The value reaches the funding
manager through funding.DevConfig, which production builds leave nil, and
the RPC server reads it from the same getter. Only an explicit static
remote key request is allowed. Default selection still never falls back
to it, and the legacy type stays rejected in every build.

The harness maps the static remote key commitment type to the new flag.
With it, we run the data loss protection test for both static remote key
and anchor channels, which covers sweeping the non-delayed to_remote output
after a force close. We also add a static remote key SCB restore case, run
the legacy revocation producer restore on a static remote key channel as
it did before, and add the type back to the altruist watchtower test. The
deprecated commit type test now uses no-anchors directly for its peer, and
still checks that a node without the dev option rejects the type.

commit.message:
itest: open anchor channels in the breach and fee rate tests

In this commit, we move the two itests that still opened static remote
key channels over to anchor channels, since lnd now refuses to open new
static remote key channels.

In the breach confirmation hint test, Mallory2 opened a static remote
key channel so that she would need no coins. With anchors, the wallet
holds back a fee-bump reserve for every public anchor channel the local
node funds, so an empty wallet would fail the open. We make the fake
funding open private instead, which skips that reserve. Alice still
registers for confirmation of the fake funding txid for a private
channel (only zero-conf channels skip that step), so the hint poisoning
path the test exercises is unchanged.

In the absurd fee rate test, the reserve case was derived from the
tweakless commitment weight. We re-derive it for anchors. The initiator
now pays both the fee at input.AnchorCommitWeight (1124) and the two
330 sat anchor outputs. With a 100,000 sat channel and a 19,999 sat
reserve, the smallest fee that leaves the initiator at or below the
reserve is 100,000 - 660 - 19,999 = 79,341 sat, which takes a fee rate
of 70,589 sat/kw. That is below the 400 sat/vbyte (100,000 sat/kw)
anchor fee cap Alice already runs with, so no cap change is needed. We
add guards that both the absurd rate and the reserve case rate sit at
or below that cap, so a lower cap fails loudly instead of quietly
changing the rate Alice proposes.

commit.message:
itest: make anchor channels the default

In this commit, we align integration tests with production by using anchor channels by default. A test-only no-anchors option remains available to exercise negotiation against peers that cannot open a supported commitment type.\n\nThe affected funding, PSBT, backup, remote signer, and watchtower tests now account for anchor outputs, wallet reserves, and sweep behavior. We also add end-to-end coverage for explicit deprecated requests and implicit fallback rejection.

commit.message:
server: only prune persistent connection when peer has no channels

The funding timeout handler pruned the peer's persistent connection
state unconditionally. A peer can have another open or pending channel
while one pending channel times out; pruning then dropped reconnect
state for a peer we still share a channel with. The brontide Start path
guards its prune with an open-channel count check; mirror that by asking
the access manager whether the peer has any open or pending channels
before pruning.

commit.message:
funding+server: release failed pending channel state

In this commit, we centralize pending-channel cleanup in cleanupPendingChannel, which closes the local discovery signal, deletes the initial forwarding policy row and deletes the channel opening state row. All three steps are idempotent, so it is safe to call from several failure paths.

We invoke it when a confirmed funding transaction fails wallet validation, when the funding timeout fires, and when the funder receives an invalid funding_signed message. The timeout path also resolves the contract so the chain arbitrator stops watching the channel and the peer is pruned from persistent reconnects.

The access manager now re-creates a missing peer score from the persisted pending count on a pending close, so an offline peer's pending channel slot is released instead of leaking temporary access until restart. The backup proxy now treats FundingTimeoutEvent as a close so the timed-out channel is removed from the on-disk backup immediately.

commit.message:
lnwire+zpay32+bolt12: enforce BOLT text validation

In this commit, we enforce the BOLT 1 text rules on every field the spec types as utf8: node aliases, BOLT 11 descriptions, and BOLT 12 offer descriptions, issuers, and payer notes. A shared ValidBoltText helper rejects invalid UTF-8, control and format characters, private use, surrogates, and the line and paragraph separators while tolerating unassigned code points.

The fixed-width V1 alias keeps its trailing NUL padding but rejects embedded NUL; V2 aliases and all invoice and offer fields validate on both read and write so locally constructed messages cannot carry banned characters either. Tests cover each banned category, malformed UTF-8, and valid non-ASCII text.

commit.message:
discovery: keep local proofs and bound future cache memory

In this commit, we stop deferring our own announcement_signatures in the evictable, in-memory futureMsgs cache. The funding manager creates our half only after its required confirmation depth and never re-sends it, so caching could permanently lose it on restart or eviction by any peer. Local halves now go straight through the normal pipeline, which durably stores them and reliably delivers them to our counterparty. Remote halves still wait for the configured proof maturity delta.

We also charge the future message cache for retained memory instead of a constant 1 per entry. Each message costs its maximum wire body plus 16 bytes per decoded feature bit, so a dense channel announcement can no longer let one peer pin ~0.7 GB. Ordinary messages keep their 1,000-entry bound, oversized entries are refused, and eviction stays LRU. Tests cover local-proof survival across restart/eviction, weighted admission/eviction, and the dense-feature memory bound.

commit.message:
funding+lnwallet: keep advertised HTLC limits valid

In this commit, we reject remote HTLC constraints that cannot produce a valid channel update: a zero in-flight maximum or a minimum above the channel capacity. This prevents accepted channels from getting stuck before their announcement.

We also cap our optional minimum HTLC preference at the remote and capacity-derived maximum. Our preference must not turn otherwise usable remote limits into an invalid update. Focused tests cover rejection at the capacity boundary and the announcement parameter clamp.
